rules: User wording is descriptive input and is never automatically persisted as an alias.
Aliases are deterministic discovery hints, not a phrase grammar.
Classify intent and domain semantically before resolving task state.
For CONTINUE with an exact current task identity, use that exact task.
For CONTINUE with a resolved domain and exactly one default-resume task in that domain, select that task even when the user's wording does not match any alias.

For SYSTEM_MAINTENANCE or selection of the UAOS controller option, inspect state/TASK_INDEX.json#controller_tasks: exact controller task identity wins; otherwise one eligible default-resume controller task is resumed; multiple defaults fail closed; no eligible controller task leaves the session at the controller root.

For material or multi-turn controller maintenance, persist controller identity/progress through the existing state/TASK_INDEX.json#controller_tasks plus state/tasks state_ref before relying on chat context for continuation.
For a bare generic CONTINUE/INHERIT request that resolves to no domain or exact task, do not guess a task: render the current inheritance selector defined by config/SESSION_INTERACTION_POLICY.json.
If the wording semantically identifies a non-default task, require enough evidence to resolve that exact task; otherwise fail closed on ambiguity.
After task selection, reread the exact domain business authority or controller maintenance state before any material action.
prohibitions: Do not add or mutate aliases because of one-off colloquial wording.
Do not route by raw keyword overlap alone.
Do not use chat memory, broad search results, or retired controller state as task authority.
Do not silently default a bare generic inheritance request to whichever task was most recently active.
Do not discard a persisted eligible controller maintenance task merely because the user first selected the generic UAOS controller option.
